subject: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?

messages.author: da88deeac332794d
messages.subject: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
parts:
Hi Shiny Devs. (Winston, Joe, etc.),

First of all, I want to to thank you for building this wonderful web framework. I've attempted to work with other frameworks in the past, and found them far more difficult to implement and use, and ultimately it was easier to just avoid them altogether. Shiny, on the other hand, has been incredibly straightforward to use and we've been able to make some powerful apps out of it already.  Notably, it's allowed me to use the analytic power of R in situations where other, more clunky, solutions were in place and create a whole lot more impact with my clients/colleagues. SO BIG KUDOS TO YOU AND THE TEAM!

For me to make full use of the software and really take it to the next level, we'll need some good and powerful authentication (all of my data is highly confidential and there's concerns in my company that web-sockets can be hacked a little easier than alternatives) and other back-end solutions to make sure the proper infrastructure is in place to share our Shiny apps outside of the intranet.  

I know you have discussed elsewhere on the forum that authentication will be part of the commercial version. Are there any other features you plan to implement that you can share with us?  Would this be a proper place to make requests for the types of features we'd hope for out of the commercial version of this software? And lastly, any ideas on when you'll be offering this or when you'll start building it up beyond the beta?

Obviously you're free to leave me/us out of this (I don't want to jeopardize you making some real money off of all the work y'all have done!), but I'd--maybe others too?--certainly love to know! 

Regards,
Aaron

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Commercial Shiny Server Timeline and Features?
parts:
We're hoping to launch a beta version of the commercial version of Shiny Server in June. It will include authentication. With your situation I imagine you will want to run Nginx, Apache, or HAProxy in front of it to provide SSL termination and shut off access to the Shiny Server port at the firewall (we will also provide SSL/TLS support directly in Shiny Server, but, it is generally a best practice to put a best-of-breed web/proxy server like the aforementioned in front of your app servers as a first line of defense).

In other words, your users will connect to e.g. Nginx via HTTPS on port 443, then Nginx will hit Shiny Server on port 3838 (or on a Unix domain socket, which will be supported soon).

We are not sure when a v1 of the commercial version will come, it really depends on the feedback we get. If the beta tag is a show stopper for you, let us know.

I don't know why websockets would be more easily hacked than regular HTTP--if you have any evidence (even the flimsiest) of that I'd love to hear it! And anyway if you are running on HTTPS then the websocket is connecting over HTTPS as well.
